title: A persistent checkpoint mirror/ledger mismatch now hides its cause behind a generic fence Deadline
outcome: When the typed checkpoint mirror/ledger refusal repeats for the same owner instead of clearing on the next coherent tick, the fences it retains end with a diagnostic that names that refusal, or the repetition is bounded, rather than ending only in a generic Deadline.
acceptance: A deterministic test makes the typed refusal repeat for one owner on every tick (for example, a session whose serialization is rejected while its ledger entry keeps changing) and shows that a retained fence's terminal result or progress report names the repeated mirror/ledger refusal, or that the refusal stops being retried after a stated bound, without shortening any fence's original deadline.
